title: Immutable bootstrap networking & staged upgrade guardrails for air-gapped VPCs
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem statement: Customers running Redwood Private in fully isolated VPCs or air-gapped datacenters require a deterministic, auditable bootstrap and upgrade path that minimizes egress, guarantees artifact provenance, and supports staged rollouts with safe rollback. This PRD defines operational requirements, networking constraints, upgrade sequencing, and measurable acceptance criteria for immutable-bootstrap and staged upgrades in offline or limited-egress environments. The goal is to enable upgrades and initial installation without introducing covert egress, while preserving safety controls (canary, telemetry, KMS rotation, operator rollback).
goals: Define a minimal networking contract for bootstrap and upgrades that works with zero direct Internet egress (mirror-based or physical media).
Specify immutable bootstrap semantics: signed images/manifests, checksum reconciliation, and operator-level verification before any node executes kubelet pulls or package installs.
Provide staged upgrade guardrails: canary subset, progressive group rollout, automated health gating, and clear rollback triggers tied to telemetry and API surface checks.
Enable customer-operable fallback paths (local mirror, removable media, or proxy) and operator runbooks for emergency rollback and artifact re-provisioning.
non_goals: Designing a bespoke on-prem artifact delivery service beyond mirror replication instructions.
Implementing application-level migration logic for customer workloads (this is infra-level upgrade safety only).
assumptions: Customers can provide at least one internal HTTP(S) mirror or brokered artifact distribution mechanism (Nexus/Artifactory/minio) OR physical media upload to the mirror.
Customers can accept signed manifests and perform offline signature verification using provided public keys or KMS attestations.
Operators have a kube-admin account and can cordon/drain nodes as needed for staged rollout steps.
networking_requirements: Minimal egress: default allowed egress blocked; only pre-approved mirror endpoints allowed during bootstrap/upgrade using an allowlist or proxy.*
DNS: support split-horizon DNS or explicit host entries to resolve internal artifact mirrors; no external DNS lookups to third-party registries during install.
MTU and path MTU discovery: document and verify recommended MTU (typically >= 1400) for artifact downloads; operator preflight includes an MTU check.
Fallback proxy: optional authenticated outbound proxy support for customers who allow controlled egress for specific artifact URLs; proxy credentials must be customer-managed.
No background telemetry or SaaS callbacks during bootstrap: telemetry uploads must be disabled by default until operator explicitly enables connectivity post-install.
bootstrap_constraints: Immutable images: all operator and runtime images must be signed and delivered with a .sha256 checksum manifest; installer verifies signatures before unpacking.
Verifiable manifests: bootstrap manifest must include image digest, signature URL, and short provenance statement (builder image + build timestamp).
Offline verification tooling: provide a lightweight tool (rbin) that validates checksums and verifies signatures against attached public keys prior to installation.
Artifact staging modes: support (1) mirror sync from Redwood-hosted registries to customer mirror, (2) customer pulls via controlled proxy, (3) physical-media import into customer mirror.
upgrade_sequence_spec: Canary group selection: support selecting 1-5% of nodes or specific operator instances as a canary cohort for the new release.
Staged batches: allow configurable batch sizes with default soft limits (25% of control plane nodes per batch).
Health gating: each batch must pass liveness checks, API responsiveness (<250ms p95 for control plane), operator readiness, and custom customer probes before proceeding.
Automatic pause & rollback: if telemetry or health checks indicate regressions (see acceptance criteria), orchestrator pauses and auto-rolls back the batch to the previous immutable image.
KMS rotation: when upgrades include KMS or credential rotation, rotation must be coordinated and reversible within the same rollout window without requiring full cluster restore.
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: Offline bootstrap success: Given a private VPC with an internal artifact mirror and no outbound Internet access, the installer completes a full bootstrap (control plane + first worker) within defined timeout (2 hours) using mirror or physical media only.
AC-02: Signature & checksum validation: Installer refuses to apply any image or manifest with mismatched digest or signature; mismatch yields a blocking error with an auditable log entry.

AC-03: Minimal egress enforcement: When operator selects "zero-egress" mode, no outbound connections to external registries or telemetry endpoints are initiated during bootstrap and upgrade. Network captures (tcpdump) should show only mirror/proxy endpoints.
AC-04: Canary safety gate: A canary cohort upgrade must run for a configurable observation window (default 30 minutes) and pass all health checks before the next batch proceeds.

AC-05: Automatic rollback trigger: If p95 control-plane latency increases >30% from baseline for two consecutive windows or if customer probes fail >=2 in 3 minutes, the orchestrator must automatically roll back the last batch.

AC-06: Operator-driven emergency rollback: Provide a documented runbook and a single operator command that reverts cluster images to the prior immutable tag within the SLA window (15 minutes to initiate work).

AC-07: Upgrade audit trail: Each upgrade must produce an immutable audit artifact listing artifacts used (image digests), who initiated the upgrade, and a verifiable signature preserved in the customer mirror or operator logs.

AC-08: Telemetry off-by-default: Telemetry collection must remain disabled during initial bootstrap and require an explicit operator toggle and documented allowlist before any outbound telemetry is sent.

AC-09: Broken-mirror mitigation: If the mirror checksum reconciliation fails for a required artifact, the bootstrap/upgrade must pause and surface a clear remediation path (re-sync, import via media, or staged fallback proxy).
AC-10: KMS rotation safety: If a KMS rotation is part of the release, rollback must restore previous KMS keys or rehydrate secrets from preserved sealed-backup artifacts without data loss.
operational_playbooks: Playbook-Install-Offline: step-by-step for mirror sync, signature verification, and initial install with troubleshooting checks (MTU, DNS, certificate trust).
Playbook-Upgrade-Canary: commands for selecting canary cohort, starting staged rollout, observing metrics, and invoking automatic rollback.
Playbook-Manual-Rollback: emergency rollback steps including draining, image re-tagging, re-initializing operator state, and validating cluster consistency.
Playbook-Checksum-Reconciliation: how to run checksum verification tools, fetch missing artifacts via physical media, and verify post-import integrity.
decisions: Use signed immutable images with SHA256 digests as the single source of truth for bootstrap and upgrade artifacts.
Default to telemetry-disabled mode for all zero-egress installs to avoid accidental data exfiltration.
Support mirror-first workflow as the primary offline distribution pattern; physical media is a documented fallback, not the primary UX.
tradeoffs: Immutable images and signature checks increase bootstrap time and operational complexity but greatly reduce supply-chain risk in air-gapped environments.
Conservative canary sizing reduces blast radius but increases time-to-upgrade for large fleets; default values balance safety and speed but remain configurable.
Zero-egress mode limits convenience of SaaS integrations (auto-update, telemetry) and shifts responsibility to the customer for mirror health and bandwidth planning.
open_questions: Q1: Should we provide a Redwood-managed mirror appliance (VM/Ova) customers can run locally to simplify mirror setup, or is that out of scope for this release?
Q2: What is the minimum mirror bandwidth we should recommend for clusters of different sizes (S/M/L)? Need to define bandwidth guidance and suggested sync windows.
Q3: Does customer legal/regulatory policy require storing signed upgrade audit artifacts in a separate WORM store? Provide guidance or integration recommendations?
